caption: Figure 4: Performance evaluation of different benchmarks on varying the amount of labeled data used for training. The x axis denotes the fraction of labeled data, whereas the y axis in the top and bottom rows denote the Micro-F 1 and Macro-F 1 scores respectively. DeepWalk and node2vec give comparable performance on PPI. In all other networks, across all fractions of labeled data node2vec performs best.
description:
This figure presents a comparative analysis of different algorithms' performance on various datasets, measured by Micro-F1 and Macro-F1 scores. The x-axis represents the fraction of labeled data used for training, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. The top row shows Micro-F1 scores, while the bottom row shows Macro-F1 scores. The algorithms compared are Spectral Clustering, DeepWalk, LINE, and node2vec. node2vec consistently outperforms the others across all datasets and fractions of labeled data, with the exception of PPI (Homo Sapiens), where it performs similarly to DeepWalk.

caption: Figure 6: Scalability of node2vec on Erdos-Renyi graphs with an average degree of 10.
description:
Section 1: A line graph showing the scalability of node2vec on Erdos-Renyi graphs with an average degree of 10. The x-axis represents the number of nodes (log10 scale), and the y-axis represents the time taken (log10 scale in seconds). Two lines are plotted: one for sampling + optimization time and another for sampling time. The sampling + optimization time line is higher than the sampling time line, with the difference increasing as the number of nodes increases.

Section 2: The figure shows the scalability of node2vec on Erdos-Renyi graphs with an average degree of 10. The x-axis is labeled as "log10 nodes" and the y-axis as "log10 time (in seconds)". Two series are plotted: "sampling + optimization time" and "sampling time". The "sampling + optimization time" line is higher than the "sampling time" line, with the difference increasing as the number of nodes increases.
